name: marketing-ideas
description: Checks whether a marketing idea can pay for the customers it brings before money is spent. From a product description it builds a context card (buyer, price, margin, demand state, existing assets), proposes one concrete idea per channel family, removes ideas that break disclosure or platform rules or lack a source of buyers, scores the rest with an evidence grade and returns one main bet plus two cheap probes. For a single idea it prints the most you can afford per customer, signup and click and whether a quoted cost fits. It writes test cards with pass and stop lines set before launch and a sample-size check, and reads channel test results with intervals. Every number is the user's or a labelled assumption.

interface.longDescription: Five skills for deciding which marketing ideas deserve money and how to tell whether they worked. Idea shortlist reads a product description, fills a context card with the buyer, price, margin, demand state and the assets the team already has, writes one concrete idea per channel family with a traffic source and a converter, removes ideas that are incomplete, break review, endorsement, email or platform rules, or fail on a cost you gave, and returns one main bet plus two probes with a not-now table. Idea ranking does the same for your own list, setting product features and content topics aside. Idea payback check takes one idea, such as a sponsorship, a booth or a launch day, and prints the most you can afford per customer, signup, click and person reached, a break-even table for a quoted cost, five failure modes and the cheapest test. Idea test card sets pass, iterate and stop lines before launch and checks whether the volume can show a result, switching to a threshold read when it cannot. Idea readout reads channel test counts with Wilson intervals, thin-sample labels and a coincidence check, and decides scale, iterate once, stop or inconclusive. No benchmarks and no invented rates: every number is yours or a labelled assumption, and every rule row carries the date it was read.
defaultPrompt: Sponsor a 3,000-reader newsletter for $1,200? $39/mo plan, 85% margin, 6-mo payback; assume 2% click, 10% trial, 40% paid.
Marketing ideas for my $39/mo stock app for indie bookstores: 85% margin, 6-mo payback, $300/mo cash, 2 founders, 140 stores.
Results: 120 cold emails, 0 replies. 18 stores via distributor reps: 5 trials, 2 paid. Scale, iterate or stop each channel?
